where: Worked example 1, steps 1 and 8 (and Section 2 block list)
problem: The example picks an 8051-family chip and then assumes an on-chip ADC: 'the ADC, timer, GPIO, program memory and RAM are all on the one chip' and 'a microprocessor would need separate ROM, RAM, timer and ADC chips'. The classic 8051 has no built-in ADC; it needs an external ADC0808/0809 (or a special variant) plus its wiring. A student would write in the exam that the 8051 has an internal ADC and lose marks.
fix: Either state that the chip chosen is an 8051 variant with an on-chip ADC, or say that the sensor feeds an external ADC whose digital outputs the 8051 reads through a port. Change step 8 to: 'The timer, GPIO, program memory and RAM are on chip; only the ADC is outside (built in on ADC-equipped variants), so a microcontroller is still the right choice.'

where: Section 1, word length paragraph, and Exam trap 3
problem: 'It is the width of the data bus' and 'the data bus width is the word length' are stated as if always true. Usually true, but not always: the 8088 has a 16-bit word with an 8-bit external data bus, and the 8086 has a 16-bit word with a 16-bit data bus. Presented as a rule, it can mislead.
fix: Say: 'Word length is the number of bits the ALU handles at a time. It is usually, but not always, the same as the data bus width — the 8088 has a 16-bit word and an 8-bit data bus.' In trap 3 keep 'n address lines give 2ⁿ locations' and drop the identification of data bus width with word length.

problem: The figure shows Flash and RAM both hanging from one system bus, which contradicts the Harvard description given just above it: an 8051-type Harvard MCU has separate program and data buses.
fix: Add a note in the figure caption/aria that in a Harvard part the Flash connects to the CPU by a separate program bus and the RAM by a separate data bus, and the single system bus shown is the simplified von Neumann view.

problem: 'It has no program memory, no RAM, no timer, no ADC and no I/O pins' — a microprocessor does have pins (address, data, control, and often serial lines); what it lacks is general-purpose parallel I/O ports, which come from chips such as the 8255.
fix: Write: 'It has no program memory, no RAM, no timer, no ADC and no general-purpose input/output ports; parallel I/O must come from an external chip such as the 8255, wired to the processor's bus.'
